label: Ubiquiti UniFi BeaconHD (UAP-BeaconHD)
description: UniFi BeaconHD mesh AP: 5 GHz 4x4 1.7 Gbps and 2.4 GHz 2x2 300 Mbps, AC wall-plug powered, Bluetooth management, no Ethernet ports.
notes: Vendor figures from the UniFi BeaconHD techspecs page: 5 GHz **4x4 1.7 Gbps**, 2.4 GHz **2x2 300 Mbps**, max 11.5 W, **universal AC input 100-240 V** - it plugs into a wall socket. **There is no Ethernet port at all**, and the management row lists **Bluetooth** only: it is a pure mesh node, so it cannot be wired, cannot be PoE-powered and cannot be provisioned over the network. In a topology it is reachable only through the wireless mesh and whatever the radio carries.

label: Ubiquiti UniFi Mobile Router (UMR)
description: UniFi Mobile Router: 2x 1G RJ45, LTE Cat 4 (150/50 Mbps), WiFi 4, PoE+ input with 10 W PoE passthrough, DIN/wall mount.
notes: Vendor figures: **(2) GbE RJ45 ports**, **LTE Cat 4** (150 Mbps down / 50 Mbps up), WiFi 4 1x1, 9 W, PoE+ (48-54 V) or USB-C or 4-pin ATX DC. The PoE row is the interesting one: **(1) PoE input and (1) PoE output, max 10 W, which requires a PoE+ switch** - so it can be powered by the switch it sits on *and* pass power through to one downstream device, but only when the upstream is PoE+ rather than plain 802.3af.

label: Ubiquiti UniFi Mobile Router Ultra (UMR-Ultra)
description: UniFi Mobile Router Ultra: 2x 100M RJ45, LTE Cat 4, WiFi 4, USB-C or 9-30 V DC, DIN/wall mount, no PoE.
notes: Vendor figures: **(2) FE RJ45 ports** - fast ethernet - **LTE Cat 4**, WiFi 4 1x1, **5.7 W**, USB-C 5 V/2 A or **9-30 V DC** on a 4-pin ATX header, **-30 to 70 C** operating. **The "Ultra" is the lesser unit**: against the UMR it drops both ports from gigabit to 100M, loses PoE entirely, and gives up LTE band coverage - in exchange for a wider DC input range, a wider temperature range and one third less power. The name does not rank the hardware.

label: Ubiquiti UniFi Gateway Pro (UXG-Pro)
description: UniFi Gateway Pro: 2x 10G SFP+ and 2x 1G RJ45 (one WAN, one LAN of each), 3.5+ Gbps routing with IDS/IPS, 1U rack, DC backup.
notes: Vendor figures from the store specification: **"(1) 10G SFP+ and (1) GbE WAN port, (1) 10G SFP+ and (1) GbE LAN port"**, **maximum WAN port count 3**, **3.5+ Gbps routing with IDS/IPS enabled**, 1U rack with DC power backup. **Four ports total on a 1U gateway** - two of them 10G cages - so the default layout is one 10G and one 1G per side, and reaching three WANs means reassigning the LAN cage. That is a reassignment, not a fifth port.
